theater: 大理羊苴咩城與洱海走廊

battle.name: 蒙古滅大理之戰
battle.theater: 大理羊苴咩城與洱海走廊
battle.brief: 1253年秋，元世祖忽必烈奉蒙哥可汗之命率軍南征，自寧夏六盤山分三路南下，循金沙江谷地直抵雲南，十一月進逼大理國都羊苴咩城。段興智遣使出降，洱海地區歸入蒙古，雲南自此成為元朝迂迴夾攻南宋的西南基地。十字弩是此役攻守的骨幹：蒙軍靠它封鎖隘道與城頭，大理諸部則以弩列陣死守城門。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 1253年的雲南，交戰的兩方是蒙古帝國與大理國。蒙古方面，大汗蒙哥坐鎮和林，以忽必烈為總統師，忽必烈自將中軍，樞密院與諸王、千戶的編制仍照草原舊制運作：每一大帳所出之兵為一軍，軍下設萬戶、千戶、百戶，什伍長層層編制，戰時結陣、戰罷解甲牧馬，後勤靠牛羊群與隨軍草料維持。兵分三路：西路由老將兀良合台統，出吐蕃取道雲南西北；中路由忽必烈自領，沿洮岷與金沙江河谷南下；東路由抄合等部循江東岸推進，並各遣使招撫沿途吐蕃、麼些、白彝諸部首領。大理方面，統治者是段氏，段興智以羊苴咩城為都，白族為主體，兼轄彝、藏、傣、白狼諸部，各部首領多為世襲土酋，按戶部曲充軍，城防依洱海與點蒼山天險，都城牆厚、濠闊，環繞民居與佛寺數十座，段氏自居宮城，另有大將高泰祥等分兵於金沙江與沿江諸隘。蒙軍以征服者的身份自居優越地位，大理則以守土者自居，兩軍的處境與心態自此不同。
countriesEn: The two sides that met in Yunnan in 1253 were the Mongol Empire and the Kingdom of Dali. On the Mongol side the Great Khan Möngke stayed at the Karakorum and named Kublai as overall commander, with Kublai personally leading the central column. The apparatus of the steppe still ran on its old decimal organisation: the troops of each darqan formed a tem, the tem was divided into mingghan, qaghan and baγutu, with file leaders below them, soldiers forming up for a battle and then returning to graze their horses afterwards, while supply was carried on herds of cattle and sheep and on the forage the animals found along the route. The army moved in three columns. The western column was led by the veteran general Uriyangqadai, who came down through Tibet along the northwestern edge of Yunnan; the central column was Kublai's own, moving south along the Tao and Min valleys and then down the Jinsha River gorge; the eastern column under Chaγa and other commanders advanced along the east bank of the river, while envoys went ahead to win over the Tibetan, Mosuo, Bai and Nuosu chiefs of the country. On the Dali side the ruler was the Duan clan, with Duan Xingzhi holding court at Yangjumie, the present city of Dali, as his capital. The state was essentially Bai, with Yi, Tibetan, Dai and other peoples under it; many local chiefs held hereditary positions and mustered their own households as soldiers. The capital's defences rested on the waters of Erhai and the heights of Cangshan, with thick walls, broad ditches, dozens of temples and residential quarters, and the Duan family kept its own inner palace, while generals such as Gao Taixiang held positions on the Jinsha River and at the passes along it. The Mongols entered as conquerors who counted themselves the superior party; Dali was defending its own land, and the two armies began from entirely different assumptions.
people: 這場戰役裡真正決定節奏的是五個人。蒙哥可汗在和林下詔，指名忽必烈領兵征雲南，理由說得很清楚：先取大理，再圖南宋，把雲南變成側翼。忽必烈帶著核心部眾與漢地幕僚同行，幕僚之中以廉希憲最見分量，進軍途中屢次勸他約束士卒、以恩信收人心，攻城之際主張保全城內廟宇、禁止士卒侵擾，兼以醫藥救治隨軍病卒，這套作風在蒙古征服史上相當少見。兀良合台是西路的統帥，這位追隨蒙古兩代的宿將走的是吐蕃、麗江一線的高原邊緣，沒有在隘口硬撞，而是用威脅與交易拆散白彝諸部的聯盟，先後迫降押赤一帶的首領摩娑，減少了正面的抵抗。汪德臣率領鞏昌路軍擔任先鋒，追索大理國主段興智直至洱海沿岸。守方的主角則是段興智本人與大將高泰祥：段興智在城破前遣使請降，保住了宗室與城中秩序；高泰祥在金沙江一線佈防，是蒙古軍西進時最硬的一道阻礙，兵敗後隨段氏一起歸順，後來仍留在雲南效力。
peopleEn: Five men really set the pace of this campaign. The Great Khan Möngke issued the order from the Karakorum, naming Kublai as the commander of the expedition against Yunnan, and stating the reason plainly: take Dali first, then move on to the Southern Song, and turn Yunnan into a flank. Kublai marched with his own core followers and a staff of Chinese and Central Asian advisers, and among them Lian Xixian carried the most weight: on the march he repeatedly urged his master to restrain the soldiers and win people over by trust, and before the assault he argued for the protection of the temples inside the city and against the troops harassing the inhabitants, while also setting up medicine for the sick among the army. Such restraint was unusual in the record of Mongol conquest. Uriyangqadai commanded the western column. This veteran of two generations of Mongol service took the highland margin through Tibet and Lijiang instead of forcing the passes head-on, breaking up the alliance of the Bai and Nuosu polities by threat and by negotiation, and forcing the surrender of local leaders such as Mosuo around the Yachi region, which removed much of the resistance in front of him. Wang Dechen led the troops of Qiangchang as the vanguard and pursued the Dali ruler Duan Xingzhi down to the shores of Erhai. On the defending side the central figures were Duan Xingzhi himself and the general Gao Taixiang: Duan sent an envoy to offer surrender before the city fell, which preserved the royal house and the order of the city, while Gao Taixiang, deployed along the Jinsha River, was the hardest obstacle the western Mongol advance met; after his defeat he submitted with the Duan house and afterwards continued to serve in Yunnan.
kits: 卡面上的十字弩是這場戰役裡最貼合的兵器。弩在十三世紀已經是成熟技術：弩機以銅鐵製成，張力由弩臂與弓弦負擔，擊發只要扣下懸刀，不必再拉一次弓弦；漢式弩機的形制在宋金以來的中原軍隊中標準化，雲南則由大理國與白彝、苗、麼些諸部廣泛使用，獵物與戰具共用同一種形制，這也是大理弩在嶺外諸蕃商路上的名氣來源。蒙古軍自身的骨幹仍是筋角複合的蒙古反曲弓，靠一人數馬的騎射與齊射壓制陣線，但攻牆、守壘、封鎖隘道這些需要站定瞄準的活計，弩更合適：一名弩手占位固定，能把箭壓在城頭或山道轉角，逼守軍縮回盾後。弓弩之間的差別在這場戰役裡被地形放大，雲南山道狹窄、坡陡，蒙古騎兵難以展開，反而要靠步行的弩手與前鋒在前面清道。攻城器械方面，蒙古人帶著自西征以來就熟悉的砲、雲梯與撞木，工匠就地取用雲南出產的銅、鐵與木料，攻守雙方都備有刀、矛、弓箭、投石與滾木。大理一方也有自己的長處：白棉布製作的甲衣與旗幟、洱海沿岸練就的水上運輸，以及佛寺中保存的銅鐘與各種金屬構件，攻城之後成為蒙古人眼中可以徵發的物資來源。
kitsEn: The crossbow on the card is the weapon that fits this campaign most closely. By the thirteenth century the crossbow was a mature technology: the lock was made of bronze or iron, the tension was carried by the bow and its string, and once cocked the shot was released simply by squeezing the trigger lever, with no need to draw the string a second time. The Chinese-pattern lock had been standardised in the armies of the Central Plains since the Song and Jin, while in Yunnan the same form was used widely by the Kingdom of Dali and by the Bai, Miao and Mosuo peoples, the very same type serving for hunting and for war, which is the source of the Dali crossbow's reputation on the trade routes beyond the ridges. The backbone of the Mongol army itself remained the horn-and-sinew composite reflex bow, whose pressure came from mounted archery and massed volleys; but for work that demanded standing still and taking careful aim, such as attacking walls, holding fortifications and sealing passes, the crossbow was the better tool. A crossbowman holds a fixed station and can lay his bolt onto a parapet or a bend in the mountain path, forcing the defenders back behind their shields. The difference between bow and crossbow was magnified by the terrain in this campaign: the Yunnan tracks were narrow and steep, cavalry could not deploy, and the work of clearing the way ahead fell to crossbowmen and other foot soldiers on the vanguard. For the siege the Mongols brought the artillery, scaling ladders and battering rams they had known since the western campaigns, and their craftsmen used the copper, iron and timber of Yunnan on the spot; both sides carried blades, spears, bows, crossbows, stones for throwing and rolling logs. Dali had strengths of its own as well: armour and banners of white cotton cloth, the water transport the lake shore had trained, and the bronze bells and metal fittings kept in the temples, which after the siege became resources the Mongols thought fit to take.
tactics: 進攻部署是典型的蒙古式多路合擊加上政治收編。第一步是不打硬仗的偵察與拉攏：兀良合台的西路在高原邊緣逐部迫降摩娑等首領，拆掉大理在西北的屏障；中路由忽必烈直取金沙江，在江面寬處以羊皮吹脹成革囊，士卒伏在囊上順流而下，人馬用此法渡過金沙江，避免了正面強渡的損失；東路則沿江東岸掃清沿途隘口與城堡，切斷大理援軍北上的通道。第二步是合圍羊苴咩城：蒙軍抵達後分屯各門之外，架設攻城塔、雲梯與撞木，砲手對著城樓與城垛轟擊，同時以弩手壓制城頭，限制守軍的射界。守方倚仗城牆厚、濠溝深，把主力放在城門與城樓段，用弓弩與滾木打退了頭幾波硬衝。第三步是政治收編：忽必烈在軍中不斷放出招降與安民之令，廉希憲主張以寬宥為主、保全城內佛寺廟宇，這使段興智在守軍士氣崩落之際得到台階，遣使請降；元軍入城之後並未縱兵大掠，而是接管城防、登記府庫、徵收糧草，按下以德服人的盤算：用最小的兵源消耗換取雲南的物產與兵源，讓這片地方的資源可以源源不斷支援下一步的對宋作戰。
tacticsEn: The plan of attack was the classic Mongol combination of converging columns and political absorption. The first step was reconnaissance and negotiation without a hard fight: along the highland margin Uriyangqadai brought one group after another to terms, including leaders such as Mosuo, and stripped away the Dali screen in the northwest; the central column under Kublai drove straight at the Jinsha River, where, at the wider stretches, sheepskins were inflated into leather bags, the soldiers lay down on them and were carried across by the current, man and horse crossing the river by this means and sparing the cost of a forced frontal ford; the eastern column swept the passes and strongholds along the east bank and cut off the route by which Dali reinforcements might march north. The second step was the encirclement of Yangjumie: on arrival the Mongols took up positions outside each gate, erected siege towers, scaling ladders and battering rams, had the artillery shoot at the gate towers and parapets, and used crossbowmen to dominate the walls and restrict the defenders' fields of fire. The defenders, trusting the thickness of the walls and the depth of the ditches, concentrated on the gate sections and tower positions and beat back the first rushes with bows, crossbows and rolling logs. The third step was political absorption: Kublai kept issuing orders to surrender and to spare the people, while Lian Xixian pressed for leniency and for the protection of the temples inside the city, which gave Duan Xingzhi a way down once the morale of the garrison had broken and led him to send out an envoy. Once inside, the Mongol troops did not give themselves over to uncontrolled plunder; they took over the defences, registered the stores and levied grain and supplies, following the calculation of winning men by virtue: buy the resources and the manpower of Yunnan at the smallest cost in soldiers, so that what the province produced could feed the next stage of the war against the Song without end.
data: 幾組可以核對的數字與距離如下。元軍出兵的規模，《元史》繫於十萬之數，這是含沿途徵發與新附軍的總數，真正投入攻城的核心兵力遠少於此，數千至一萬餘人的說法比較接近實際。時間軸清楚：1253年九月，忽必烈率軍出六盤山；十月抵金沙江，革囊渡江；十一月兵鋒抵達洱海；十二月初大理工城歸降，段興智遣使出降。前後不足四個月，行程自寧夏六盤山至雲南大理逾兩千里，途中翻越高山、峽谷與高原，糧秣靠牛羊群隨軍牧養與沿途徵發維持。攻城歷時數日，具體戰損史無明文，只知元軍在強攻城門時有折損。編制上，蒙古騎兵每人備二至三匹馬、一張弓與數十支箭，攻城與山地戰中另配弩手；弩的有效射程約在一百至二百步之間，一次上弦只能發一箭，裝填遠慢於拉弓，因此只適合守點與封路，不適合野戰中的密集射擊。大理城牆依山勢築成，護城壕寬數丈，牆面可容並馳的馬道，城內人口以萬計。糧食一項，蒙古人自帶牛羊，漢地幕僚則更依賴沿途徵收的米麥與茶馬交換，這在雲南山區意味著必須同時控制驛道與渡口。
dataEn: A few figures and distances can be checked. The size of the Mongol force is given in the Yuan Shi as a hundred thousand, but that total includes men raised on the march and newly submitted contingents; the core actually engaged at the siege was far smaller, and a figure of several thousand to something over ten thousand is closer to the truth. The timetable is clear: in September 1253 Kublai led his army out of the Liupan Mountains; in October he reached the Jinsha River and the troops crossed on inflated leather bags; in November the vanguard reached the shores of Erhai; in the first days of December the city of Dali submitted and Duan Xingzhi sent his envoy. In under four months the army covered more than two thousand li from the Liupan Mountains of Ningxia to Dali in Yunnan, crossing high ridges, gorges and plateau country, with grain and fodder carried on herds of cattle and sheep driven along with the column and supplemented by requisitions on the way. The siege itself lasted several days; no text records the losses in detail, though the Mongols are known to have suffered men in the repeated assaults on the gates. In organisation, each Mongol horseman carried two or three horses, one bow and several dozen arrows, and crossbowmen were added for the siege and the fighting in the hills. A crossbow had a useful range of roughly one hundred to two hundred paces, fired only one bolt for each cocking of the mechanism, and took far longer to reload than a drawn bow, which is why it served to hold points and seal roads rather than to deliver massed fire in open battle. The walls of Dali were built along the line of the hills, the ditch before them several zhang across, the wall walk broad enough for horsemen to ride abreast, and the population inside the city counted in the tens of thousands. As for food, the Mongols carried their own cattle and sheep, while the Chinese staff relied far more on rice, wheat and tea-horse trade gathered along the route, which in the Yunnan mountains meant that the roads with their post stations and the river crossings had to be held at the same time.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是蒙古帝國本身的戰略：大汗蒙哥志在滅宋，但南宋的四川防線堅固，正面仰攻代價太高，必須迂迴。雲南的大理國控制著從西藏高原到中南半島的南北通道，又盛產戰馬，一旦拿下大理，蒙古軍就能從滇西出兵，與正面的四川形成夾攻。所以這場戰爭不是臨時起意，而是整個滅宋計畫的第一步。中層是大理自己的態度：段氏自開國以來名義上臣服於中原王朝，蒙古崛起後也接受了蒙古的使者，卻始終保留獨立的官署、軍隊與賦稅，拒絕出兵助蒙古攻宋，也拒絕交出通道。兩邊使節往來時屢受折辱，蒙古軍過境又向大理索取糧秣以供大軍消耗，段氏陽奉陰違，關係迅速惡化。最內層是忽必烈的個人算盤：他以藩邸舊部與漢地幕僚為核心的兵力出征，一旦打下大理，就掌握一支直屬自己的南方軍隊、一處可以徵發馬匹與銅料的產地、一份穩定的賦入，這套獨立的軍政與財源，正是他後來與阿里不哥爭奪汗位的本錢。雲南的佛國氣象對崇尚釋教的大汗和汗弟同樣有吸引力：以招撫與寬宥換取歸順，在忽必烈看來比大規模攻城更划算。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause behind the fighting. The outermost was the strategy of the Mongol Empire itself. Möngke meant to destroy the Southern Song, but the Song defences in Sichuan were strong and the cost of attacking them head-on was high, so the campaign had to be turned. The Kingdom of Dali controlled the north-south corridor running from the Tibetan plateau to the Indo-Chinese peninsula and was famous for its warhorses; once Dali was taken, the Mongols could march out of western Yunnan and attack Sichuan in a pincer with the front. The war was therefore no sudden impulse but the first step of a plan to finish the Song. The middle layer was Dali's own conduct. Since its founding the Duan house had nominally submitted to the dynasties of the Central Plains, and it accepted Mongol envoys after the empire rose, yet it kept its own offices, army and taxes, refused to send troops to help the Mongols against the Song and refused to hand over the corridor. The envoys on both sides were repeatedly slighted, and when the Mongol army passed through Dali it demanded grain and fodder to feed the host, which the Duan house pretended to supply while obstructing. Relations soured quickly. The innermost layer was Kublai's own calculation. He went into the field with an army built around the old soldiers of his own princelike household and his Chinese staff; if he took Dali he would hold a southern force of his own, a province from which horses and copper could be drawn, and a steady revenue, and that independent military and financial base was exactly the capital he would later use to contest the khanship against Ariq Böke. The Buddhist kingdom of Yunnan also attracted the Great Khan and his brother, both inclined to the religion: for Kublai, a negotiated submission bought by clemency looked cheaper than a storm of the walls.
impact: 這場戰爭結束之後，雲南的局面徹底改寫。第一是行政層面的根本變化：段氏王國覆亡，蒙古人在雲南先設宣慰司，由賽典赤贊思丁等漢地回回官員主持，把這片從來沒有被中原王朝直接編入行省的土地掛進了中央的版圖，稍後才正式設為雲南行省。行省之下仍以段氏與白彝、麼些諸部首領為土司，蒙古人靠以土官治土省掉大量行政成本，但也從此把雲南變成雙重統治的實驗場。第二是軍事層面的連鎖反應：雲南從此成為元朝向西南擴張的基地，往後攻交趾、三征緬甸、平定滇西與滇南的諸部，兵源與糧秣都從滇中抽調；反過來看，南宋也從此丟失了西南屏障，長江上游與兩淮之間的縱深只剩下襄陽與四川兩個支點。第三是經濟與工藝層面的流動：雲南的銅、馬、茶成為元廷的戰略物資，銅被大量調運去鑄錢與造砲，漢地工匠的冶鐵、造紙、鑄銅技術順著官道進入雲南，帶動了滇中手工業。第四是族群與信仰的重新排序：大理以白族為主、佛教興盛的城市生活被打散，段氏宗室遷居京師，廟宇與銅鐘被接管後成為統治象徵，洱海地區從此進入長達數百年的土司、衛所與流官交錯的時代，直到明代設洱海衛，這中間衝突的根源都埋在那幾年裡。
impactEn: When the war was over the situation in Yunnan had been written over from top to bottom. First came a fundamental administrative change: the Duan kingdom was extinguished, the Mongols first set up a pacification commission in Yunnan under men such as Sayyid Ajjal Shams al-Din, and brought a land that no Central Plain dynasty had ever administered directly into the empire's order, later to be made a full province. Beneath the province the Duan house and the chiefs of the Bai, Mosuo and other peoples remained as native administrators, and the Mongols saved a great deal of administrative expense by ruling through local lords; but from that moment Yunnan became an experiment in dual government. Second came a chain of military consequences. Yunnan was now the base from which the Yuan court expanded to the south-west; the campaigns against Jiaozhi, the three expeditions against Burma and the reduction of the tribes of western and southern Yunnan all drew troops and provisions out of the province. In the other direction, the Southern Song had lost its south-western screen, and the depth between the upper Yangtze and the Two Huai was reduced to the two points of Xiangyang and Sichuan. Third came the movement of goods and crafts. The copper, horses and tea of Yunnan became strategic resources for the Yuan court, with copper carried away in quantity to be cast into coin and cannon, while the techniques of the Central Plain in ironworking, papermaking and bronze casting travelled along the official roads into Yunnan and gave an impulse to the craft industries of the central plateau. Fourth came a reordering of peoples and faiths. The urban civilisation of Dali, Bai in the main and strongly Buddhist, was broken up; the Duan royal house was moved to the capital of the empire; the temples and their bronze bells passed to new hands and became the emblems of a new rule. The Erhai region entered several centuries in which native lords, military garrisons and appointed officials took turns, until the Ming established the Ehai Guard, and the roots of the conflicts of that age were planted in these very years.
result: 結果很簡單：大理國亡了。段興智出降，羊苴咩城的城門在1253年十二月的某一天對元軍打開，延續了三百多年的段氏白族王國就此終結。段氏宗室被遷置京師，授官封爵但不再擁有洱海的統治權；蒙古人沒有把雲南併入草原的怯薛體系，而是留兀良合台等將領鎮守，把雲南變成元朝前線的軍政基地。忽必烈在1254年前後率主力北返，留下的人繼續經營滇中，同時把目光轉向四川與襄陽，這才是這場戰爭真正的目的。對元軍而言，這是一次代價極低、收益極高的征服：沒有打消耗掉主力的大會戰，卻一次解決了馬匹、銅料、糧食、兵源四個瓶頸，換來的是隨時可以向西南與南方用兵的支點。對大理而言，則是一個獨立的、以白族為主、有著自己文字與信仰秩序的國家，就此被併入一個以草原為中心的帝國，段氏數百年的經營被改寫為帝國南方的一處府庫與兵源。歷史記載有限，具體的攻城細節與兩軍的損失數字都無從核實，但可以確定的是：從1253年起，雲南再沒有獨立的王朝，蒙古的旗幟在洱海邊立了起來，而在此後數百年的時局裡，這片土地始終是中原王朝最南端的邊疆，也是最難以整合的一角。
resultEn: The outcome was simple: the Kingdom of Dali ceased to exist. Duan Xingzhi surrendered, the gates of Yangjumie opened to the Mongol army on some day in December 1253, and the Duan house's Bai kingdom, which had run for more than three hundred years, came to an end. The royal family was moved to the imperial capital and given offices and titles, but no longer held authority over Erhai. The Mongols did not fold Yunnan into the keshig system of the steppe; they left generals such as Uriyangqadai to hold it and turned the province into a military and administrative base for the Yuan frontier. Kublai led the main body north again around 1254, while the men he left behind worked the middle valley of Yunnan and turned their attention towards Sichuan and Xiangyang, which was the true purpose of the whole war. For the Mongols this was a conquest of very low cost and very high return: no great battle was fought to exhaust the main army, yet horses, copper, grain and manpower were solved in a single stroke, and what they gained was a pivot from which they could strike to the south-west and the south at any time. For Dali it was the end of an independent state, Bai in the main, with its own script and its own religious order, swallowed by an empire with its centre in the steppe; several centuries of Duan achievement were rewritten as a treasury and a recruiting ground on the southern edge of that empire. The record is thin, and the details of the assault and the losses of either army cannot be checked; what is certain is that from 1253 onward there was no independent dynasty left in Yunnan, the Mongol banners were planted on the shores of Erhai, and for the centuries that followed this land remained the southernmost frontier of the Central Plain dynasties and the hardest of them to integrate.
